title: `PrefilterDb::from_path` can place a record in an empty split file
body:
`PrefilterDb::from_path` in `mmseqs.rs` reads a prefilter or align db that mmseqs may leave split over files `name.0`, `name.1`, and so on. It takes each `.index` offset as a position in the concatenation of those files. It sums the file sizes into `prefix_sum`, the start of each file, and finds the file holding a record by binary search:

```rust
let file_idx = match prefix_sum.binary_search(&offset) {
    Ok(idx) => idx,
    Err(idx) => idx.saturating_sub(1),
};
```

mmseqs leaves zero-size files in the split. A run of `mmseqs align --threads 8` on a 24-query fixture left these file sizes and starts:

| file | size | `prefix_sum` |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 17699 | 0 |
| 1 | 0 | 17699 |
| 2 | 16485 | 17699 |
| 3 | 0 | 34184 |
| 4 | 0 | 34184 |
| 5 | 26775 | 34184 |
| 6 | 20066 | 60959 |
| 7 | 17930 | 81025 |

An empty file starts where the next file starts, so `prefix_sum` holds that value more than once. A record at the start of the next file has that offset, and `binary_search` may return any of the matching entries. Rust's docs leave the choice unspecified.

If it returns an empty file, the record's relative offset is 0 in a file with no bytes. The null-terminator check in `from_path` then fails at `read_exact`, and nail stops with an error. nail would not read a wrong record. In 21 runs on that fixture the lookup returned the right file every time.

The check ran against mmseqs `8cc5ce3`. mmseqs computes the offsets in `DBWriter::mergeIndex`, which adds the size of each earlier thread file to the offsets of the next. The scratch files are in `tmp-claude/2026-10-14-prefilter-index/` on Jack's machine.

## Proposal

Take the last file whose start is at or below the offset:

```rust
let file_idx = prefix_sum.partition_point(|&s| s <= offset) - 1;
```

mmseqs writes every record with at least its null terminator, so a record never starts at the end of the data. The last file starting at or below a record's offset is then never an empty one.
close_reason: Fixed in `9a671f7` on `libsail-io`: `from_path` finds the file with `partition_point`, which returns the last file starting at or before the offset.
